extras.ask:
Spiderweb can use free Python packages that aren't installed yet:

{list}

Spiderweb works without them, just slower. Install them now? (needs the internet; it can take a few minutes)

If you say No, Spiderweb won't ask again.
extras.numba: Numba: much faster with lots of notes (zooming, moving shapes, letting go)
extras.pillow: Pillow: images shown faster, and the Image tool opens JPG, WebP, BMP and TIFF too
extras.installing:
Installing {name}…

This can take a few minutes. Spiderweb opens when it's done.
speed.loops_readme:
Spiderweb's compiled loops (the Numba speed-ups), saved so the next start has them at once instead of making them again.

Safe to delete: Spiderweb makes them again when they're missing (that takes a few seconds, while it works at the slower speed).
A new Spiderweb version or another PC makes new ones by itself.

join_split.split_into_separate_shapes_or: Split into separate shapes (or Ctrl+Z) gives the old shapes back.
join_split.turned_the_shape_into_a_live: Turned the shape into a live shape (Split into separate shapes gives it back)
join_split.turned_shapes_into_a_live_sha: Turned {n} shapes into a live shape (Split into separate shapes gives them back)

join_split.select_one_shape_to_split_it: Select one shape to split it.
join_split.text_and_pasted_notes_can_t: Text and pasted notes can't be split.

join_split.only_joined_curves_and_custom: Only joined curves and custom shapes split into separate shapes.
join_split.merged_done: Merged: each key row slid in until it met the other shape's notes.
join_split.merge_no_meet: No key row of these shapes meets the other's notes: nothing merged.
join_split.merge_no_image: Images can't be merged (they keep their own colours): nothing merged.
join_split.merged_left: Merged. {n} key rows had nothing to meet: they're a shape of their own now ("Merge leftovers").
join_split.merged_left_one: Merged. 1 key row had nothing to meet: it's a shape of its own now ("Merge leftovers").
join_split.split_here_use_slice: This piece was flipped, turned or sliced through its notes after its own pages: Split here can't tell which notes go where. Use the Slice tool (K) across its notes
join_split.cant_rejoin: Pieces sliced through their notes only join with the pieces beside them, cut from the same shape (moved together, if at all)
join_split.split_back_into_the_old_shape: Split back into the old shapes
join_split.made_complete: A complete shape now: its notes follow its own line
join_split.made_complete_n: {n} complete shapes now: their notes follow their own lines
join_split.plain_nothing: Nothing to turn into plain notes: the selected shapes make no notes
join_split.plain_done: Turned {n} shapes into plain notes, each note on the channel it had
join_split.plain_done_one: Turned the shape into plain notes, each note on the channel it had
join_split.slice_nothing: The slice line didn't cross any shape it can cut (lines, curves, arcs, custom shapes, funnels and pasted notes; not pictures). To cut text, merged shapes or Hz bass, turn them into plain notes first (right-click → Turn into plain notes)
join_split.slice_partly: A shape is only cut when the slice line goes all the way across it. To cut just the rows the line touches, turn it into plain notes first (right-click → Turn into plain notes)
join_split.slice_merged: A merged shape can't be sliced. Turn it into plain notes first (right-click → Turn into plain notes), then slice it
join_split.slice_merged_too: . {n} merged shapes stay whole: turn them into plain notes first to slice them
join_split.slice_merged_too_one: . 1 merged shape stays whole: turn it into plain notes first to slice it
join_split.slice_missed_notes: Pasted notes are only cut where the slice line goes through notes or between a row's notes
join_split.slice_partly_too: . {n} shapes weren't crossed all the way, so they stay whole
join_split.slice_partly_too_one: . 1 shape wasn't crossed all the way, so it stays whole
mask.tick_tip: While ticked, whatever you draw becomes a mask: a preview that shows the shapes under it only inside it (the rest faint). Nothing is cut: the shapes under it stay whole and still sound. Works with Live shape too (paint with the mask).
mask.preview_tip: Ticked: masks preview their cut, the parts of the shapes under them outside the mask drawn faint. Unticked: the shapes under masks are drawn whole, only the masks' dashed lines show. Nothing changes in the sound or the file either way, and Apply mask works the same.
mask.label: Mask: {label}
mask.panel_tip: A mask shows the shapes under it only inside it; the rest is drawn faint. The shapes under it don't change and still sound. Untick to make it a normal shape again.
mask.own_tip: Ticked: the mask's own notes sound like any shape's, as a border. Unticked: it's a pure cutter, only its dashed line shows.
mask.thickness_tip: How thick the band round the mask's notes is, in keys. It's even all the way round, in the proportions the piano roll had when the shape became a mask. With Inside it widens the inside past the outline (0 = just the inside).
mask.thickness_solid: A Fill or Spam mask shows its whole inside, so it has no thickness.
mask.show_tip: Inside: the shapes under it show inside its outline, between its own notes. Along the line: only in a band round its line.
mask.invert_tip: Ticked: the shapes under the mask show everywhere except inside it, like a cookie cutter making a hole.
mask.apply_tip: Makes a new shape of the notes the mask shows, exactly as you see them. The shapes under it don't change, and the mask stays, so you can move it and apply it again. While Own notes sound is ticked, its border notes are copied too. A mask in a group applies the whole group. Invert masks over the same shape apply together: one copy with all their holes.
mask.apply_nothing: Nothing applied: no notes show through the mask
mask.apply_done: Made {shapes} holding {notes}, as the mask shows them; the shapes under it didn't change
mask.mode_tip: How this mask joins the masks above it in its group (Shapes list order, top first). Add: the pattern also shows inside this one. Subtract: this one cuts it away. Intersect: only where this one and the ones above overlap.
mask.mode_first: The first mask in a group always adds.
mask.combine_done: Combined: {n} masks now work as one group. Set each one's Mode in the side panel
mask.separate_done: Separated: each of these masks works on its own again

paste.title: Paste colours
paste.intro: Paste any text with colours in it (a whole settings file is fine):
paste.legend: Blue = the colours that will be used.   Grey = found, not used.   Struck out = switched-off line, skipped ({n}).
paste.lock: Lock them: the image uses exactly these colours (right-click a colour later to free it)
paste.start: Only a starting point: Spiderweb may change them to fit the image better
paste.ch10_left: Channel 10 isn't used (drums): the image gets the other 15.
app.tools_list_tip: Every drawing tool. Pick one and this button shows it, so one click picks it again. The pin on a tool's right gives it its own button here.
app.pin_tip: Pin: give this tool its own button in the toolbar. Click again to take the button away.
app.keeps_overlaps_every_note_exactly_as:
Keeps overlaps.
Every note exactly as the shapes make it, all on one channel.
Notes on the same key can overlap or start on the same tick.
app.removes_overlaps_all_on_one_channel:
Removes overlaps, all on one channel.
Where two notes on the same key overlap, the earlier one is cut
where the later one starts, and the later one is stretched
to where the earlier one would have ended.
Notes starting on the same tick become one note: the loudest wins,
and it's as long as the longest of them.
app.a_channel_per_overlap_shapes_whose:
A channel per overlap.
Shapes whose notes overlap go on different channels, each on its own
track (channel 10 is skipped). Shapes that don't clash share a channel.
The box below picks what counts as an overlap.
app.split_same_key_at_the_same: Split: same key at the same time
app.split_any_notes_at_the_same: Split: any notes at the same time
app.ch10_order_tip:
Shapes take channels 1, 2, 3 … 16 in order, so a shape's 10th colour goes on channel 10.
Off: channel 10 comes last (1-9, 11-16, then 10), so ticking Use channel 10 changes no colour.
When 10 or more channels are in use, the 10th and later change colour when this is switched,
because each channel keeps its own colour. Saved with the project.
app.pad_rounds_tip:
On: each time the colours repeat, all 15 channels (16 with channel 10) get a track in the MIDI file
and Export to Domino, empty tracks for the colours that time doesn't use.
Off: only tracks with notes are written. Every note keeps its channel and colour either way.
Saved with the project.
app.new_rounds_tip:
When a shape's colours start again from the first colour, the repeated colours go on new channels
with the same colours (15 channels further on, 16 with channel 10). A channel never holds a colour twice,
so each repeat can be edited on its own in other programs. Counts for Colours, Nested and Tiles fills,
Add between steps and Copy along a path's colours. Other shapes keep the first channels.
Saved with the project.
app.pasted_15: {n} pasted shapes had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project doesn't use channel 10).
app.pasted_15_one: 1 pasted shape had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project doesn't use channel 10).
app.pasted_picture_15: {n} pasted images had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project's images don't use channel 10).
app.pasted_picture_15_one: 1 pasted image had 16 colours: brought down to 15 (this project's images don't use channel 10).
app.use_ch10_tip:
Shapes may use channel 10 too, so there are 16 colours instead of 15.
Many synths play channel 10 as drums (with a piano-only soundfont, MIDI players stay silent there).
Built-in BASSMIDI plays it as a piano. Saved with the project.
app.same_key_shapes_only_get_split:
Same key: shapes only get split when they play the same key at the same time.
Any notes: shapes get split whenever their notes play at the same time,
even on different keys (e.g. two parallel lines, or lines starting on the
same tick). Shapes that follow one after another still share a channel.
snap.tip:
The grid points and notes snap to while you draw and drag (Shift = don't snap).
Note lengths: 1/4 = a quarter note (one beat), 3/8 = a dotted quarter, 1/6 = quarter-note triplets.
Custom… = any length you set up.
snap.kind_tip:
Empty = one plain note (16 = a 16th note), the left number isn't used.
/ = that many notes (3 / 16 = three 16th notes).
. = a dotted note (one and a half notes), .. = double dotted (one and three quarters).
snap.divided_by_tip: Splits the length into this many equal steps (3 = triplets).
app.history_tip: The History list: every change as a step; click one to go back to it.
app.every_tip_searchable_opens_at_the: Every tip, searchable. Opens at the tool you're using.
app.formula_tip: Drag a line like Linear: a pattern (Wave, Zigzag, Bounce or one you saved) swings the velocity up and down around it. Its settings show next to the tool buttons; changing them changes the line you just drew.
app.ctrl_flat_shift_snap_enter_done: Ctrl = flat · Shift = snap · Enter = done · select a shape to edit only its notes
app.a_ppq_of_or_more_many:
A PPQ of {PPQ_WARN} or more: many MIDI programs can't open the file.
Spiderweb still writes it.
app.edo31_tip:
Shows the piano roll in 31-EDO: 31 keys an octave instead of 12 (key 0 = C0).
White keys = the 7 plain notes, black keys = sharps and flats, grey keys = half sharps (^) and half flats (v).
Only the look changes: the saved MIDI keeps the same key numbers.
app.edo31_audio_tip:
Playback and right-drag listening sound in 31-EDO too, every key up to 255.
Only with Built-in BASSMIDI as the MIDI out.
app.edo31_audio_needs_builtin:
Audio is ticked, but the MIDI out isn't Built-in BASSMIDI, so playback plays the usual way (keys above 127 are skipped).
Pick Built-in BASSMIDI under MIDI out to hear 31-EDO.
app.edo31_audio_builtin_only: 31-EDO Audio only works with Built-in BASSMIDI: playing as usual.
app.128_the_standard_keys_0_127:
128: the standard keys 0–127, which every MIDI program reads.
256: keys 0–255, for players that support them (handy for tunings like 31edo).
Many MIDI programs can't read keys above 127, and playback here skips them (unless 31-EDO Audio is on).
app.builtin_settings_tip: Built-in BASSMIDI's settings: the soundfont, the voice limit, and lowering it by itself when the processor can't keep up.
app.voices_tip:
How many sounds Built-in BASSMIDI can ring at once (1000 to start). More = fuller in busy parts, but more work for the processor: if playback breaks up ("Overloaded" in red next to the Settings button), lower it.
Past the limit, the oldest sounds are cut.
bs.title: Built-in BASSMIDI settings
bs.change_tip: Pick another soundfont (.sf2 / .sfz). The Hz bass preview uses the same one.
bs.guard: Lower it by itself when overloaded
bs.guard_tip: Ticked: while the processor can't make the sound fast enough (it stops or crackles), the voice limit is lowered until it keeps up, then quickly raised back to yours once it's calm. Each Play starts from your limit (moving the play line while it plays keeps the lowered one).
bs.limiter_tip: Ticked: sound louder than full volume is turned down instead of clipped (clipping = a harsh, broken sound in busy parts), so busy parts sound cleaner but flatter. Off: too loud is clipped. Heard at once.
bs.limiter_slow: Without the optional speed-up Numba, playback may break up for a moment while you edit with it on.
app.pick_soundfont_title: Pick a soundfont for Built-in BASSMIDI
app.where_copied_and_pasted_notes_start:
Where copied and pasted notes start:
First note at tick 0: the first note lands right on the cursor / play line.
From the bar line: the empty space from the bar line before the first note
comes along, so the notes keep their place in the bar.
app.domino_paste_tip:
Paste from Domino: the notes copied in Domino (Ctrl+C there) become one shape here.
It starts at the play line, like pasting in Domino (see the start setting above).
Every track's notes go into the one shape; controllers and other events are left out.
Ticks are taken as they are: use the same PPQ here.
Ctrl+V pastes them too, when they were copied last.
app.domino_export_tip:
Export to Domino: saves every note as a Domino song file (.dms), next to the MIDI file
in the Output file box, with the same name.
It can hold a PPQ up to 65535 (a MIDI file stops at 32767).
Each channel gets its own track, like Generate MIDI.
app.ctrl_shift_c_copies_the_selected:
Copy to Domino (Ctrl+Shift+C): copies the selected shapes' notes (all notes when nothing is selected).
In Domino, paste with Ctrl+V at the cursor, or double-click in the piano roll.
Multi channel: each channel goes into its own track, from that one down.
Ticks are copied as they are: use the same PPQ there.
The other way: notes copied in Domino paste here with Ctrl+V or a Select double-click.
app.glued: Glued touching notes: {notes} → {after}. The shape remembers it: right-click → Remove glue takes it off
app.velocity_drawn_in_the_velocity_pane: Velocity drawn in the velocity pane. Typing a start/end here goes back to a straight ramp.
app.starts_exactly_on_the_last_point: starts exactly on the last point
app.too_many_points: Too many points to list ({n}): drag them on the piano roll.
app.ppq_must_be_a_whole_number: PPQ must be a whole number from 1 to 65535
app.bpm_must_be_a_number_at: BPM must be a number, at least 4
app.beats_per_bar_must_be_a: Beats per bar must be a whole number from 1 to 32

Are you sure you want to delete all {n} shapes?
(Ctrl+Z can bring them back.)
app.are_you_sure_you_want_to_one:
Are you sure you want to delete the shape?
(Ctrl+Z can bring it back.)
app.copied_shape_s_ctrl_v_pastes: Copied {n} shapes — Ctrl+V pastes them at the play line, a Select double-click on empty space where you click. Paste the text anywhere to share them
app.copied_shape_s_ctrl_v_pastes_one: Copied 1 shape — Ctrl+V pastes it at the play line, a Select double-click on empty space where you click. Paste the text anywhere to share it
app.too_long: ({chars:,} characters: may be too long to paste in some places)
app.couldn_t_share: (couldn't put them on the clipboard as text to share: another program has it open)
app.shared_newer: This shared text was made by a newer Spiderweb. Update Spiderweb to paste it.
app.shared_broken: The shared text on the clipboard is cut off or changed, so it can't be pasted. Copy the whole line again.
app.shared_left_out: {n} of the shared shapes couldn't be read, so they were left out. They may have been made by a newer Spiderweb: update Spiderweb to paste them.
app.shared_left_out_one: 1 of the shared shapes couldn't be read, so it was left out. It may have been made by a newer Spiderweb: update Spiderweb to paste it.
app.shared_made_short: (made by Spiderweb {version}: may look a little different)
app.clipboard_busy: Couldn't paste: another program has the clipboard open. Try again.
share.made_older: This was made by an older Spiderweb ({version}). Some things may have changed since, so it may look a little different than it did there.
share.made_newer: This was made by a newer Spiderweb ({version}). Some things may have changed since, so it may look a little different than it did there. Updating Spiderweb makes sure it comes out right.
app.shared_drawing: The clipboard holds a shared drawing. Open the drawer and press Import to add it to your saved shapes.
big_ask.title: Spiderweb
big_ask.notes: This makes about {n:,} notes, which can make Spiderweb slow.
big_ask.domino: This copies {n:,} notes: pasting that many can make the program you paste into slow.
big_ask.dms: This saves {n:,} notes for Domino: opening a file with that many can make Domino slow.
big_ask.memory: It needs about {need} GB of memory ({free} GB free now).
big_ask.wont_fit: It needs about {need} GB of memory, but only {free} GB is free now: it will likely fail, or make this PC very slow. Closing other programs frees memory.
big_ask.drums:
This copies {tracks} tracks. In Domino they go into the track you pick and the ones below it, so the 10th one lands 9 tracks below it. If that track plays on channel 10, most players play its notes as drums.

Copy anyway?
big_ask.dont_ask: Don't ask again until Spiderweb is closed
big_ask.out_of_memory: There wasn't enough memory to do this, so nothing was changed. Closing other programs frees memory.
big_ask.out_of_memory_somewhere: Spiderweb ran out of memory, so what you just did may not have finished. Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes it back. Closing other programs frees memory.
panel_custom.one_long_note_per_key_insid: One long note per key inside.
panel_custom.the_inside_filled_with_back: The inside filled with back-to-back notes of one gate.
panel_custom.just_the_outline_chopped_in: Just the outline, chopped into notes of one gate.
panel_custom.nested_tip: The inside filled with smaller and smaller copies of the shape, one inside the other. Each step gets a colour of its own (with Multi channel).
panel_custom.nested_notes_tip: Fill: one long note per key in each step. Spam: chopped into notes of the spam gate.
panel_custom.nested_way_tip: Scaling: each copy is a true smaller copy, shrinking toward the centre point (drag its handle on the piano roll). Even band: every step is equally thick all the way round and follows each bend, like the Outline gate (no centre point). Blend: the steps follow the outline near the edge and round off smoothly into the centre point.
panel_custom.nested_of_tip: What the smaller copies are: the shape itself, or another shape from your library, made to fit the same box. The shape itself stays the outermost step.
panel_custom.nested_morph_tip: The steps change from this shape into the picked one bit by bit: the first step is this shape, the last step is the picked one. Each piece goes with the nearest piece of the other; pieces left over shrink away or grow out of nothing.
panel_custom.nested_angle_tip: Turns the copies by this much, round the centre point, before anything else. Turn adds its turn on top.
panel_custom.nested_mix_tip: 0 % = the same as Even band. 100 % = the steps round off fully into the centre point. Values in between mix the two.
panel_custom.nested_steps_tip: How many copies. The shape itself counts as the first one.
panel_custom.nested_last_tip: How big the last, smallest copy is. 0 % = the copies shrink down to a point.
panel_custom.nested_spacing_tip: 0 = even steps. Above 0: the steps get closer together toward the last copy. Below 0: closer together near the outline.
panel_custom.nested_turn_tip: Each copy is turned a little more than the one before it (measured as the shape was first drawn).
panel_custom.nested_colours_tip: How many channels the steps take turns over. Each one is a colour of its own with Multi channel.
panel_custom.nested_skip_tip: Leaves every other step without notes, so the copies show as separate rings.
panel_custom.tiles_tip: The inside filled with another shape repeated like wallpaper, cut where it meets the outline. Each tile gets a colour of its own by where it is (with Multi channel). Drag the small handle to slide the tiles.
panel_custom.tiles_of_tip: The shape every tile is made of, from your library. It fills the tile's box.
panel_custom.tiles_keys_tip: How many keys tall one tile is.
panel_custom.tiles_length_tip: How long one tile is, in ticks.
panel_custom.tiles_gap_keys_tip: Empty keys between one row of tiles and the next.
panel_custom.tiles_gap_tip: Empty ticks between two tiles side by side.
panel_custom.tiles_layout_tip: Grid: the tiles in straight rows and columns. Bricks: every other row moved half a tile sideways, like a brick wall.
panel_custom.tiles_flip_tip: Flips every other tile, so neighbours mirror each other. Both: every other row upside down and every other column side to side.
panel_custom.tiles_by_tip: Which colour each tile gets, by where it is: the next colour along each diagonal, column or row, a checkerboard (2 colours), or one colour for all.
panel_custom.tiles_colours_tip: How many channels the tiles take turns over. Each one is a colour of its own with Multi channel.
panel_custom.tiles_whole_tip: Leaves out every tile the outline cuts, so only whole tiles are left.
panel_custom.tiles_too_many: Too many tiles for this shape, so it's left empty. Make the tiles bigger or the gaps wider.
panel_custom.tiles_needs_multi: Tiles get their colours only with Channels set to Multi channel.
panel_custom.nested_needs_multi: Nested steps get their colours only with Channels set to Multi channel.
panel_custom.ripples_tip: Rings that grow out from the shapes drawn inside the outline, each one a bigger copy of its shape. Where the rings of two shapes meet, the smaller one wins. The outer outline only cuts the rings off; with no outer outline they grow out freely. Each ring gets a colour of its own (with Multi channel).
panel_custom.ripples_steps_tip: How many rings, counting the ones inside the drawn shapes.
panel_custom.ripples_grow_tip: How big the biggest ring is, compared with the shape as drawn. Greyed while Auto is ticked.
panel_custom.ripples_trim_tip: The rings stop at the outer outline. Off: they grow past it, as far as Grow to says (Auto can't be used then). Cut them by hand with the Slice tool.
panel_custom.ripples_auto_tip: The biggest ring grows just far enough to fill the whole outline. Only with an outer outline and Cut at the outline ticked.
panel_custom.ripples_turn_tip: Each ring is turned a little more than the one inside it. The ring on each drawn shape stays as drawn, and the rings inside it turn the other way.
panel_custom.ripples_spacing_tip: 0 = even rings. Above 0: the small rings closer together. Below 0: the big rings closer together.
panel_custom.ripples_colours_tip: How many channels the rings take turns over. Each one is a colour of its own with Multi channel. The ring just inside each drawn shape is always the first colour.
panel_custom.ripples_skip_tip: Leaves every other ring without notes, so the rings show as separate bands.
panel_custom.ripples_edge_tip: A ring always ends exactly on each shape you drew, so its outline shows in the pattern. Off: the rings are spread evenly and may run across it.
panel_custom.ripples_inside_tip: What goes inside the drawn shapes. Rings: the rings carry on inside them. Empty: no notes inside them. Plain: one colour inside them.
panel_custom.ripples_none: Draw a closed shape for the ripples to grow from.
panel_custom.ripples_picked_tip: The shape inside whose centre point you clicked on the piano roll. Its rings can turn their own way and grow from their own spot.
panel_custom.ripples_picked_turn_tip: How this shape's rings turn: the same as all (Turn above), the other way round, or by their own amount.
panel_custom.ripples_picked_centre_tip: Where this shape's rings grow from, in the shape's box: u = 0 % at its left side to 100 % at its right, v = 0 % at its bottom to 100 % at its top. Drag its centre point on the piano roll, or right-click it to put it back in the middle.
panel_custom.ripples_needs_multi: Ripples get their colours only with Channels set to Multi channel.
panel_custom.borders_tip: Where two areas of different colours meet (coloured in the drawer's Areas tool), the notes there go to the outline too. Off: the outline is only where the filled part ends.
panel_custom.too_many_colours: This shape needs {n} colours, but a shape can have at most {most} (the outline and the plain fill count too). The extra colours share the last one.
panel_custom.normal_all_its_notes_togeth:
Normal: all its notes together.
Outline: the notes along the edge of what's filled go on a channel of their own
and the inside's on another (the same gate, so they line up). Needs Channels: Multi channel.
panel_custom.channels_isn_t_multi_channe: Channels isn't Multi channel now, so it's all one channel (turns orange).
panel_custom.fill_and_spam_where_outline:
Fill and Spam: where outlines overlap, the overlap is left empty
(a shape inside a shape makes a hole). Off: everything the lines close in is filled,
overlaps and holes too, also where one line crosses itself.
panel_custom.each_key_s_notes_start_at:
Each key's notes start at that key's left edge,
so the left side is exact and the right side ragged.
panel_custom.every_note_sits_on_the_gate:
Every note sits on the gate grid counted from the start of the song,
so the notes form straight columns (lined up with bar lines and
other shapes); both sides are a little ragged.
panel_custom.centred_tip:
What doesn't fit a whole gate is shared between both ends of each key,
so a peak or a point comes out the same on both sides.
panel_custom.range_tip: Opens a window where the gate can go from one number to another across the shape (left to right, low to high or top to bottom), along a graph you can change. Every whole-tick gate in between gets an equal share, like a gate distribution: most notes get the short gates.
panel_custom.gate_ranged_tip: A gate Range is on: the gate goes from {a} to {b} ticks across the shape (Range… changes it). Changing this number takes the Range off, back to one gate for every note.
panel_custom.ends_tip:
What happens to the bit of each key that doesn't fit a whole gate.
Pictures of each: Help (F1) → Inside fill.
panel_custom.edge_tip:
Makes the outline at least this thick, so it doesn't get thin where the shape is steep. 0 = off.
It grows into the inside, so the shape's edge stays where it is. Where the shape is thinner than that, all of it becomes outline.
Works with Empty, Outline spam, and Fill / Spam set to "Outline". Lines that don't close have no inside and stay as they are.
panel_custom.edge_mode_tip:
Even band: the inside shrinks the same way on every side, top and bottom too, measured as the shape looked when it was first drawn (so a circle shrinks into a smaller circle), so the outline is equally thick all round, holes and inner corners included.
Grow sideways: each short outline note just grows longer toward the middle of its key.
colours.shift_tip:
Each key row starts on a different channel: every few keys up, the turns start this many channels later, so one colour makes slanted lines instead of straight stripes.
0 = off. 1 = one way, -1 = the other way; bigger numbers make flatter lines, more keys make steeper ones.
Rows are counted from the shape's lowest key. Works with Each key row too.
colours.rows_tip:
From its start: each key row starts again at the first channel where its notes begin, so the colours follow the shape's left edge instead of making straight stripes.
From its end: each key row's last note gets the first channel, counting back, so the colours follow the shape's right edge (exact with Ends: Stretch or a short gate).
A row with a gap (like a ring's two sides) starts again after the gap too.
Spam and Outline spam shapes only.
colours.rows_only: None of the picked shapes is Spam or Outline spam: Fill, Empty and lines have one note per piece of a key row, so every note would start again (one colour).
colours.tip:
The notes take turns over several channels, so the colour changes with each turn (which colours you see depends on the program showing the MIDI).
By step: each step the next channel (spam: each gate column; lines: each note in time).
By key: each key the next channel (rows).
By time: a note length from the start of the song, like the snap (1/4 = a beat), so it lines up with the bar lines.
Channels: how many take turns. Every: how long one channel lasts.
Needs Channels: Multi channel.
colours.needs: Channels isn't Multi channel now: all its notes are in one channel, so the colour doesn't change.
panel_custom.hz_not_merged: Not on a merged shape (Gate sensitive merge): split it first.
panel_custom.hz_tip:
Spam so fast that the repeats sound like a tone.
The gate is worked out from the tone, the BPM and the PPQ, and gates of two sizes
(like 34 and 35 ticks) are mixed so the tone comes out exact. Every key is in step.
Best heard after the MIDI is rendered to an audio file.
panel_custom.hz_skipped: Some of the selected shapes are Hz bass. A Hz bass gets its gate from its tone, so it stays as it is: only the other shapes change.
panel_custom.hz_range_off: A gate Range doesn't work together with Hz bass, so it's switched off. Unticking Hz bass brings it back, with the gate it had.
panel_custom.hz_cents_tip: Pitch adjustment: 100 cents = one key up, -100 = one key down.
panel_custom.hz_short: The gates are short, so the tone wobbles: a higher PPQ fixes it.
panel_custom.hz_stale: The BPM changed since this Hz bass was made, so its tone is off now.
panel_custom.hz_gates_tip:
Auto: Fixed for a note that holds still when it's off by no more than the threshold,
else Alternating. A slide is always Alternating.
Alternating: gates of two sizes take turns, so the tone is exact.
Fixed: every gate is the same whole number of ticks, so the tone is a little off
(the higher the PPQ, the less).
panel_custom.hz_notes_tip:
Opens the Hz bass window: place notes there and the tone follows them.
Notes at the same time make a chord; the red line is the tone you really hear.
panel_custom.hz_short_fixed: The gates are short, so the tone is off: a higher PPQ fixes it.
panel_custom.hz_tool_info: Drag up or down on the piano roll where the Hz bass should start: that is the keys it repeats. Then place its notes in the window that opens.
panel_polygon.points_tip: How many corners (3 = triangle, 4 = square, 5 = pentagon…), or how many points a star has.
panel_polygon.kind_tip:
Polygon: straight sides, a flat side at the bottom.
Star: outer and inner points take turns.
Crossing star: every Skip-th point joined by straight lines that cross (5 points, skip 2 = a pentagram).
panel_polygon.inner_tip: Star: how far out the inner points are, in % of the outer ones (smaller = thinner points, 100 = a polygon with twice the points).
panel_polygon.skip_tip: Crossing star: each point is joined to the one this many points further round (1 = a plain polygon). When it shares a divisor with Points it makes several loops (6 points, skip 2 = two triangles).
panel_custom.they_keep_their_own_velocit: They keep their own velocities until you change the velocity here or in the velocity pane.
panel_custom.drag_a_corner_or_side_to: Drag a corner or side to stretch them, just outside a corner to turn them, just outside a side's middle to skew them.

panel_custom.ends_that_nearly_touch_1_64:

panel_custom.one_gap_in_the_outline_fill: One gap in the outline: filled as if the dashed line closed it.

Font size: the number is the font size in keys, like a font size anywhere
(capital letters come out smaller than that).
Rows: capital letters are exactly that many keys tall.

panel_text.extra_room_between_letters_in:

panel_text.room_between_lines_in_of_the:
Room between lines, in % of the font's own line spacing.

How much of a key's height has to be inside a letter for that key to play there
(Fill / Spam only). 50% = the key's middle. Lower = chunkier letters, higher = thinner.
panel_text.makes_the_letters_strokes_thi:
Makes the letters' strokes thicker, in keys (minus = thinner),
as the text looked on screen when it was typed. Big values can look odd in tight corners.
panel_text.pick_the_font_you_can_type: Pick the font (you can type its name in the window that opens).
panel_text.direction_tip:
Which way the letters go.
Piano roll: along time, reads normally here.
Player across: reads across the keys in a falling-notes player; each new line arrives before the one above it.
Player down: the letters arrive one after another in steady steps, first letter first;
each new line is a column beside it (higher keys), arriving at the same time.
The player choices set Letter turn to 90 and tick Flip letters, so the letters stand upright in a player.
panel_text.letter_turn_tip:
Turns each letter on its own spot (anticlockwise, as the piano roll shows it).
90 with Flip letters ticked = upright in a falling-notes player.
panel_text.flip_letters_tip: Turns each letter upside down before Letter turn turns it.

help.about.title: About Spiderweb
help.about.tip: Version, license, and where Spiderweb keeps your files.
help.about.words: about version license copyright author credits folder errors log website github download update source bug report look dark mode light theme
help.welcome.title: Welcome to Spiderweb
help.welcome.tip: Draw lines and shapes on the piano roll and they become notes. Pick a tool at the top; a short tip like this one explains each the first time. F1 or the Help button: every tip, searchable.
help.whats_new.title: What's new
help.whats_new.tip: What changed in each version, newest first.
help.whats_new.words: new changes changelog release notes version update
help.select.title: Select (V)
help.select.tip: Click a shape to select it, drag it to move, drag its squares to reshape. Drag empty space = select with a box, click empty space = move the play line. Double right-click = to the last drawing tool and back.
help.select.words: move pick choose drag box rectangle marquee area double right-click switch toggle last tool
help.line.title: Line (L)
help.line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click the start and then click the end.
help.poly.title: Polyline (P)
help.poly.tip: Click point after point (or drag each piece). Double-click or right-click to finish.
help.free.title: Freehand (F)
help.free.tip: Drag to draw. Straighten (panel) turns it into perfect lines, curves or shapes.
help.free.words: draw hand pencil smooth straighten shape recognition
help.curve.title: Curve (C)
help.curve.tip: Drag from start to end (or click both), then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click the curve to add an anchor.
help.arc.title: Arc (A)
help.arc.tip: Click the start, a point it passes through, and the end. Or drag from start to end, then move the mouse to bend it and click.
help.custom.title: Custom shape (S)
help.custom.tip: Pick a shape in the panel (or make one with Drawer…), then drag a box to place it.
help.box.title: Circle and Polygon (O / Q)
help.box.tip: Drag a box (or click two corners). Ctrl = a perfect circle or polygon as it looks. Polygon: pick the points and kind (polygon, star, crossing star) in the panel.
help.box.words: rectangle ellipse oval shapes square triangle polygon pentagon hexagon star pentagram hexagram
help.funnel.title: Funnel (N)
help.funnel.tip: Draw its line, then its wall (drag, or click twice each). Then middle-click on the line to start a curve there.
help.text.title: Text (X)
help.text.tip: Click on the piano roll and type. Esc = done. The letters become a custom shape.
help.hz_bass.title: Hz bass (H)
help.hz_bass.tip: Drag up or down on the piano roll where it starts (the keys it repeats), then place notes in the window that opens: spam so fast it sounds like those tones. The red line there is the tone you really hear.
help.picture.title: Image (I)
help.picture.tip: Turns an image (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP…) into notes in up to 15 colours. Set it up in the window that opens, then drag it into the piano roll.
help.picture.words: picture image photo png gif pixel art drawing colours colors palette dither dithering blend blending spread pattern detail details mouth eyes sharpen brightness contrast saturation falling piano roll player preview original keys steps hex

help.hz_notes.title: Placing notes (Hz bass)
help.hz_notes.tip: In the Hz bass window, press the mouse to place a note and drag it; drag either end to change its length. Select (V) draws a box around notes.
help.hz_notes.words: hz bass place notes pencil select box drag move resize length copy paste delete snap zoom scroll
help.hz_tone.title: Tone and tuning (Hz bass)
help.hz_tone.tip: The red line is the tone you hear. Zoomed in, drag it in a note to tune that note. Gates: Alternating = exact, Fixed = a little off.

help.hz_shape.title: Hz shape (Hz bass)
help.hz_shape.tip: Hz settings… → Hz shape…: draw where the keys hit inside each wave, and set how long each note lasts. Same pitch, different look.

help.hz_slides.title: Slides (Hz bass)
help.hz_slides.tip: To make the tone slide from one note to another: select both, right-click → Slide between the selected notes. Or middle-click one note, then the other.
help.hz_slides.words: hz bass slide slides glide portamento bend middle-click dots curve s-curve double single handle bend tool per-note pitch scoop fall
help.hz_layers.title: Layers and loudness (Hz bass)
help.hz_layers.tip: Layers (in the Hz bass window's toolbar) shows the layers list: each layer has its own notes and its own sound. Loudness shows a pane to draw how loud each note and layer is.
help.hz_layers.words: hz bass layers layer mute solo rename colour copy sound move clash channel loudness loud velocity fader volume mixer line
help.hz_preview.title: Preview (Hz bass)
help.hz_preview.tip: Preview plays this Hz bass alone through Spiderweb's own synth with your soundfont. Grey over the notes = not made yet.
help.hz_preview.words: hz bass preview listen hear play synth soundfont sf2 sfz voices voice limit reverb chorus volume grey render
help.hz_effects.title: Effects (Hz bass)
help.hz_effects.tip: Effects are lines in the pane under the notes: click an effect's name to put it on, then drag its points.
help.hz_effects.words: hz bass effect effects line point points automation repeat repeats loop lfo pump sidechain amount depth bypass mute pencil draw curve bend tension hold step select copy paste shape
help.hz_envelope.title: Once per note and sustain (Hz bass)
help.hz_envelope.tip: An effect can start over at every note, like a synth's envelope, and wait at a sustain point until the note ends.
help.hz_envelope.words: hz bass envelope adsr once per note restart retrigger stretch drop rise pluck kick 808 sustain release fall hold point diamond
help.hz_effect_list.title: Every effect (Hz bass)
help.hz_effect_list.tip: What each Hz bass effect does, one line each.

help.live.title: Live shape (G)
help.live.tip: Lines, curves, arcs, freehand and boxes you draw now go into ONE custom shape. Close its outline to fill it. Right-click empty space to start the next one.
help.turn_live.title: Turn into live shape (Ctrl+R)
help.turn_live.tip: Select lines, curves, arcs (or custom shapes) and press Ctrl+R: they become one live shape, so they can be filled. Split into separate shapes (Ctrl+Shift+G) gives them back.
help.turn_live.words: convert live custom fill combine group lines curves arcs
help.fill.title: Inside fill (custom shapes)
help.fill.tip: Empty = just the outline. Fill = one long note per key inside. Spam = back-to-back notes of the gate. Outline spam = the outline chopped into notes of the gate. Ends = what to do with the bit that doesn't fit a whole gate. Outline (box next to Fill / Spam) = the edge on its own channel.
help.fill.words: spam gate empty inside outline gap hole overlap cancel union hz bass tone pitch cents colour color area border thick outline gate band sideways
help.nested_tiles.title: Nested and Tiles fills
help.nested_tiles.tip: Nested = the inside filled with smaller copies of the shape, one inside the other, each step its own colour. Tiles = another shape repeated like wallpaper inside. Both are picked under Inside and need Multi channel for their colours.
help.nested_tiles.words: nested steps copies shrink smaller scale scaling even band blend round centre center point handle turn spiral rings morph angle tiles tile wallpaper repeat pattern grid bricks flip checkerboard whole
help.ripples.title: Ripples fill
help.ripples.tip: Rings that grow out from the shapes drawn inside a custom shape's outline, each ring a bigger copy of its shape and a colour of its own. Picked under Inside, needs Multi channel for its colours.
help.ripples.words: ripples rings ring grow source sources frame outline heart star waves meet seam steps colours spacing turn spiral grow auto cut past edge free centre center point handle picked other way empty plain
help.custom_edit.title: Custom shapes: resize, turn, skew
help.custom_edit.tip: Drag a corner or side to resize, just outside a corner to turn, just outside a side's middle to skew. Drag inside to move it.
help.tumours.title: Tumours
help.tumours.tip: Bumps along the line: size, length, distance apart, rotation, which side. Length 0 = spikes (a zigzag). The … next to a number = a graph, so it changes along the line. Bumps take the current zoom's shape: zoom first, then set them up.
help.tumours.words: bumps spikes zigzag wave zoom round stretched rotate tilt lean slant trapezoid graph grow shrink change along formula
help.claw.title: Claw machine
help.claw.tip: Changes the selected shapes' notes: cuts slices of time out, or keeps some notes and trashes some. The shape stays as drawn, so you can move it, or open the claw again to change it or use it once more on top. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.claw.words: thin out remove delete notes pattern trash skip every other rhythm chop stutter slice gap speed up slow down bouncing ball random stripes columns shorten
help.path.title: Copy along a path
help.path.tip: Click on the piano roll where the path ends (B): the shape is copied along the path, and the copies follow the mouse until you click. Drag the points or the round middle points to bend it. The shape stays as drawn. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.path.words: copy copies repeat array duplicate along path line curve arc trail steps stairs grow shrink spacing formula wave flip mirror keep inside range plain
help.strum.title: Strum
help.strum.tip: Makes the notes of each chord start one after another, like strumming a guitar: a straight edge of notes becomes a slope or a curve. The shape stays as drawn. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.strum.words: strum guitar arpeggio slope stairs staircase lean slant chord spread humanize delay velocity fade alternate up down chop
help.chop.title: Chop
help.chop.tip: Cuts every note into a rhythm: even pieces, swing, off-beat, or one you draw. The shape stays as drawn. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.chop.words: chop cut slice rhythm stutter swing off beat gallop triplets accent pieces split notes quick chop snap repeat
help.slice.title: Slice (K)
help.slice.tip: Drag a straight line across shapes to cut them there. With a Select box drawn first, only what's inside the box is cut.
help.slice.words: slice cut knife split divide chop scissors cut in two line plain notes freeze finalise
help.glue.title: Glue
help.glue.tip: Notes touching on the same key become one long note: fewer notes, the shape looks the same. Draw a Select box first to glue only the notes inside it.
help.glue.words: glue join merge combine fewer notes less note count reduce long notes touching
help.sustain.title: Sustain
help.sustain.tip: Each key's notes are held on until the last note of their group ends, piling up on top of each other: made for lagging out MIDI players. Holes in the shape stay empty, so it keeps its look.
help.sustain.words: sustain hold held long notes overlap overlapping stack pile lag laggy player gap holes length at most stop stops every points past end line lines drag beats ticks
help.masks.title: Masks
help.masks.tip: A mask shows the shapes under it only inside it, without cutting them: they stay whole and still sound. Apply mask makes a new shape of what shows. Combine masks to add, subtract or intersect them.
help.masks.words: mask masks preview cut cutter cookie hole invert reveal brush apply masked notes combine group add subtract intersect border
help.gate_flip.title: Gate aware flip
help.gate_flip.tip: Only the way the gates are laid out is flipped: each key row is laid from its right end, colours and velocities turned round with it. The drawing and every row's start and end stay where they are.
help.gate_flip.words: gate aware flip gates reverse mirror range right edge jagged colours order spam pasted notes runs
help.straighten.title: Straighten (freehand)
help.straighten.tip: 0 = as drawn. Higher = straighter lines, smoother curves, perfect shapes.
help.straighten.words: smooth perfect recognise shape freehand sensitivity
help.curves_pen.title: Curves: anchors and handles
help.curves_pen.tip: Drag a round anchor to move it, drag a handle dot to bend. Alt = sharp corner. Right-click an anchor to remove it.
help.curves_pen.words: bezier pen anchor handle bend corner
help.symmetric.title: Symmetric halves
help.symmetric.tip: Right-click a curve: one half follows the other, mirrored (an arch) or turned (an S).
help.join.title: Join and split
help.join.tip: Select several lines, polylines, freehand strokes, curves or arcs, then press Ctrl+G (or right-click). Right-click any of them → Split here cuts it in two.
help.join.words: join merge combine connect split cut separate pieces break apart
help.merge.title: Gate sensitive merge
help.merge.tip: Select two shapes, right-click → Gate sensitive merge: each key row of one shape slides over until it meets the other shape's notes.
help.merge.words: merge gate sensitive meet slide rows key row edge leftovers combine
help.funnel_curves.title: Funnel curves
help.funnel_curves.tip: Middle-click the line: a new curve start. Middle-click near a curve: an anchor. Select tool: click a curve again to highlight it (Del, right-click = shapes, linking).
help.funnel_curves.words: curve start anchor link mirror formula highlight
help.funnel_links.title: Linking funnel curves
help.funnel_links.tip: Linked curves change together (Ctrl while dragging = only this one). To link: Select tool, click a curve, Ctrl+click another, right-click → Link curves.
help.funnel_links.words: link linked unlink mirror mirrored flipped same shape together follow group ctrl
help.formulas.title: Formulas: shapes and patterns
help.formulas.tip: Right-click a curve, line, polyline or arc → Formula: give it a shape (Circle, Spiral, Heart…) or a pattern along it (Wave, Zigzag, Square wave, Spikes…). Live shape strokes, drawer strokes, funnel curves and polygon sides have it too.
help.formulas.words: formula math preset expression shape pattern wave zigzag bounce square sawtooth teeth spikes stairs swell fade spiral circle heart flower loop custom symmetric mirrored arch turned
help.undo.title: Undo and redo
help.undo.tip: Made a mistake? Ctrl+Z = undo, Ctrl+Y = redo. Tick History in the toolbar to see every change as a step and jump back to any of them.
help.undo.words: undo redo ctrl+z ctrl+y ctrl+shift+z mistake back
help.history.title: History (undo steps)
help.history.tip: Every change is a step in the History list (tick History in the toolbar: it shows between Project and Shapes). Click a step to go back to it; Undock puts the list in a window of its own.
help.history.words: undo redo history steps back undock
help.selecting.title: Selecting, copying, flipping, turning
help.selecting.tip: Drag a box on empty space with Select, Ctrl+click = more shapes, Ctrl+A = all. Ctrl+C / V = copy / paste at the play line. Ctrl+H / J = flip, Ctrl+Left / Right = turn 90°.
help.selecting.words: box rectangle marquee area stretch scale resize copy paste duplicate flip mirror rotate turn undo redo delete
help.sharing.title: Sharing shapes
help.sharing.tip: Ctrl+C also copies shapes as one line of text: paste it anywhere to share them. Ctrl+V pastes a shared line. In the drawer: Export / Import.
help.sharing.words: share sharing export import clipboard text send friend code paste copy
help.shapes.title: Shapes list
help.shapes.tip: The Shapes list (side panel) shows every shape with its note count. Click a row to select it; Duplicate, Delete and Delete all are under it. Further down the list = on top.
help.shapes.words: list rows order layer top duplicate delete all count
help.numbers.title: Number boxes
help.numbers.tip: Drag a box's name sideways to change it, or press Up / Down in the box. Shift = big steps, Ctrl = small steps.
help.numbers.words: scrub drag value arrow wheel math
help.view.title: Scrolling and zooming
help.view.tip: Wheel = scroll, Shift+wheel = sideways, middle-drag = scroll. Ctrl+wheel = zoom (Ctrl+Shift = time only, Alt = keys only). Fit view (top) = see everything.
help.view.words: zoom scroll pan fit view snap grid quantize quantise triplet dotted custom
help.velocity.title: Velocity pane
help.velocity.tip: Draw velocities over the bars: Linear, Curve, Pencil or Formula. With a shape selected only its notes change.
help.hz_live.title: Live keys (Hz bass)
help.hz_live.tip: This sound is NOT your MIDI. The live keys play a quick copy that Spiderweb makes from your soundfont's own notes, so you can try a Hz bass before placing it. Only notes you place in the Hz bass window go into your MIDI. It can sound a little different from a real render, most with soundfonts that change their sound at random.

help.hz_osc.title: OSC tab (synth window)
help.hz_osc.tip: The OSC tab's knobs set the sound the way most synths do: Volume envelope, two oscillators (OSC A and OSC B), Pitch, Vibrato / Tremolo, Tone and Character.

help.hz_voice.tip: Voice = copies of the sound, a little out of tune with each other, plus Glide and Legato. Arpeggio plays every note as a fast run.

help.hz_fx.title: FX and Draw tabs (synth window)
help.hz_fx.tip: FX = a rack of Chorus, Flanger, Echo, Reverb and Compressor look-alikes. Draw = the effects' lines for one note, big.

help.playback.title: Playing and listening
help.playback.tip: Space = play / stop. Right-drag = listen to the notes under the mouse.
help.playback.words: play sound listen midi out scrub audio
help.channels.title: Channels
help.channels.tip: As drawn = everything kept. Single = one channel, overlaps fixed. Multi = overlapping shapes on different channels (each its own track).

help.files.title: Saving and MIDI export
help.files.tip: Your work saves itself. Generate MIDI writes the .mid file set under Project.

help.settings.title: Settings
help.settings.tip: The ⚙ button: look, note colours, sound, updates, tips and language, kept for every project.

help.domino.title: Copy to / Paste from / Export to Domino
help.domino.tip: Ctrl+Shift+C copies the notes; paste them in Domino with Ctrl+V. Notes copied in Domino paste here as one shape with Ctrl+V.
help.domino.words: copy paste clipboard domino track bar ppq import pasted notes export dms song file
help.drawer.title: The drawer
help.drawer.tip: Draw a shape for your library, Save it, then Use on the piano roll. Closed outlines can be filled.
help.drawer_select.title: Drawer: Select and editing
help.drawer_select.tip: Drag a point (small squares) or a stroke. Drag on empty space = a box selecting several. Del = delete.
help.drawer_select.words: drawer edit move copy flip turn
help.drawer_line.title: Drawer: Line
help.drawer_line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click both.
help.drawer_poly.title: Drawer: Polyline
help.drawer_poly.tip: Click points (or drag each piece). Click the first point again to close it.
help.drawer_free.title: Drawer: Freehand
help.drawer_free.tip: Drag to draw. Let go near the start to close it.
help.drawer_curve.title: Drawer: Curve
help.drawer_curve.tip: From start to end, then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click it = new anchor.
help.drawer_arc.title: Drawer: Arc
help.drawer_arc.tip: Click start, a point it passes through, end. Or drag start to end, then click to bend.
help.drawer_square.title: Drawer: Square
help.drawer_square.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect square.
help.drawer_circle.title: Drawer: Circle
help.drawer_circle.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect circle.
help.drawer_erase.title: Drawer: Eraser
help.drawer_erase.tip: Click a stroke to remove it, or drag a box: every stroke it touches goes. Ctrl+Z = undo.
help.drawer_areas.title: Drawer: Areas
help.drawer_areas.tip: Click an area to give it the colour picked on the right (or Empty), or drag across several. Right-click = back to normal.
help.drawer_areas.words: drawer area colour color channel fill paint bucket zone track
help.drawer_slice.title: Drawer: Slice
help.drawer_slice.tip: Drag a line across strokes to cut them there. A circle or square is cut only when the line goes all the way through it.
help.drawer_slice.words: drawer slice cut knife split scissors trim delete part
help.shortcuts.title: Keyboard and mouse shortcuts
help.shortcuts.tip: Every key and mouse shortcut in one list.
